comparison: Both evaluate core ExA-SPIM technical specifications (C11-C18, C27-C28, C44-C48, C60-C62, C164) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval groups these with imaging approach claims (C50-C56), while peer review includes these imaging claims in the same result. Both affirm the system's impressive field of view, working distance, resolution, and throughput capabilities with convincing evidence.

OpenEval evaluates imaging approach and sensor specifications (C50-C59) as SUPPORTED in a separate result. Peer review includes overlapping claims (C50-C56) in their comprehensive technical assessment (R1) as SUPPORTED. Both affirm the axial sweeping method, sensor specifications, and SNR performance.

Both evaluate the tissue processing and expansion protocol (C71-C83) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of protocol steps and validation across tissue types. Peer review accepts the expansion protocol as part of the overall ExA-SPIM methodology with convincing evidence, noting it is optimized for whole mouse brains.

Both evaluate mouse brain imaging application (C84-C86, C92-C96) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes C117 (manual tracing) in this result as SUPPORTED. Peer review addresses C117 separately (R6) as UNCERTAIN, noting insufficient evidence for automated tracing but accepting manual tracing demonstrations. Both affirm imaging quality and neuron tracing capabilities.

Both evaluate macaque brain imaging (C98-C103) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the challenging nature of primate tissue and successful axon tracking in down-sampled data. Peer review implicitly accepts these findings through overall positive assessment, describing the work as impressive and representing a leap over existing microscopes.

Both evaluate human brain tissue imaging (C108-C112) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights novel structural observations about white matter organization and feasibility demonstration. Peer review accepts the human tissue results as part of the overall demonstration, describing the data as stunning with no specific concerns raised.

Both evaluate software and data handling infrastructure (C64-C66) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the custom software development with GitHub links and throughput specifications. Peer review explicitly notes the acquisition software suite as part of the impressive work with no concerns raised.

Both evaluate the theoretical framework for expansion-assisted imaging (C119-C135) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges C135-C136 note the framework is speculative requiring further investigation. Peer review accepts the conceptual and technical novelty of using metrology lenses, with overall positive assessment supporting the claimed advantages.

Both evaluate dual-channel imaging capability (C97) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes validation of achromatic correction across visible wavelengths demonstrated in Figure 4. Peer review implicitly accepts this through overall positive assessment of macaque imaging, which includes multi-channel capabilities.

Both evaluate automated segmentation claims (C118) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes preliminary status with no quantitative comparison data. Peer review explicitly states the manuscript would be stronger with data justifying automated tracing claims, though accepts the amended text now more closely matches supporting data for manual tracing.

OpenEval evaluates future applications and cleared brain imaging (C152-C157) as UNCERTAIN, noting C153-C154 are supported by Figure 2 supplement 7 but other claims are speculative. Peer review evaluates cleared tissue imaging capabilities (C63, C153-C154) as SUPPORTED, accepting this as an additional application without questioning it.

OpenEval evaluates photobleaching characterization (C59) as SUPPORTED within the imaging approach result (R2), demonstrated in Figure 2 supplement 6. Peer review (R9) also evaluates photobleaching (C59, C145) as SUPPORTED, with no concerns raised about high laser powers, implicitly accepting the characterization.

Both evaluate photobleaching and signal collection (C139-C148, including C145) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges signal collection limitation but notes demonstrated ability to detect dim features and photobleaching characterization. Peer review accepts the overall performance without raising concerns about photobleaching or high laser powers.

OpenEval evaluates optical engineering context and metrology lens rationale (C29-C43) as SUPPORTED, establishing etendue concept, commercial objective limitations, and metrology lens properties. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific background claims.
